chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqbah, from Muyassir, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام saying: “Whoever follows the جنازة of a Muslim will be given, on the Day of Resurrection, four intercessions, and he does not say anything except that the angel says: ‘And for you is the like of that.’”

key_terms.الْمَلَكُ: the angel who responds with a similar supplication for the person
key_terms.جَنَازَةَ: the funeral bier or funeral procession of the deceased
key_terms.شَفَاعَاتٍ: intercessions granted as a reward in the Hereafter
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim believer whose funeral is being accompanied
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when final recompense is given

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for following the funeral of a Muslim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the virtue of accompanying the funeral of a Muslim and the great reward attached to it in the Hereafter. It also indicates that the supplications or words said on such an occasion are answered by an angel who prays for the same good on behalf of the speaker.
